target_customer: Security, legal, GRC and sales teams at B2B software companies that must answer customer security questionnaires and RFPs
problem: Answering customer security questionnaires and RFPs depends on scarce subject matter experts and slows deals; Wolfia's AI agent drafts cited answers from the company's own knowledge sources.
product_category: AI agent for security questionnaires, RFPs and customer contract review

founders.name: Naren Manoharan
education: Master's in Computer Science (AI and machine learning), institution not listed
founders.background_notes: YC page: led infrastructure engineering teams at Wealthfront. Page lists no other founders.

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrieval and drafting over a company's documents with integrations to Drive, Notion, Slack and portals. In 2022 the LLM tooling was less mature, so accuracy was harder; a small team could still build it.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and a stored answer library create some lock-in, but the underlying approach is copyable and many vendors later offered questionnaire automation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later comparison pages show many vendors (Conveyor, SafeBase, Vanta, Loopio) in this space; no acquisition of Wolfia found.

market_need_then: Security questionnaires were a recurring sales bottleneck for B2B vendors; evidence at the time of founding was not found in dated sources.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and plain-spoken, practical copy using concrete outcome figures.

brand_strength.rationale: Only company-published blog and case studies found; a different product also named Wolfia exists, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Wolfia is Active and still publishing in 2026, with named customers such as Amplitude, Miro and Handshake on its site and integration partnerships with Oneleet and AmplifyGRC. Funding beyond a YC convertible note is not public, so growth scale is unknown. Crowded competition from Conveyor, Loopio and Vanta and LLM commoditisation are the main risks.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights lists a 0.5M convertible note on 2022-09-07 with Y Combinator (single aggregator); one listing names Khosla Ventures and Page One Ventures as investors (aggregator only). No later round found, so coverage is partial at best. Competition list left empty: searches returned only 2023 to 2026 vendor comparison pages and a 2023-10 TechCrunch story on Conveyor, more than a year after the batch, so no source dated near the batch was found. Company website named no competitors. Name collision with another product called Wolfia. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. The website testimonial names a David Paffenholz as CEO and co-founder, which appears to be a customer, so he is not listed as a founder. Update: the $500K convertible note dated 2022-09-07 is now recorded as a round (stage other) on a single database (CB Insights). Crunchbase and the company site name Khosla Ventures, PageOne VC and Twenty Two Ventures as backers without round details, so the history is partial.
